intended_object: Composition of morphisms in the subcategory `P.Comma L R Q W` of the comma category `L ↓ R`. Its objects are those whose structure map satisfies P. Its morphisms are comma morphisms whose left component satisfies Q and whose right component satisfies W. The docstring and the `Category` instance just below it say this is what the definition is for.
explanation:
Composition works component by component: the left component is `f.left ≫ g.left` and the right one is `f.right ≫ g.right`. This is the usual composition in a comma category, and it is the same as `CategoryTheory.Comma.comp`. The commuting square is inherited from that underlying comma composition, via `toCommaMorphism`.

The two property fields hold because Q and W are closed under composition. The only hypotheses are `IsStableUnderComposition` on Q and W, which is exactly what composition needs. Identities and the rest of the multiplicative structure are only assumed later, for the `Category` instance.

There is no degenerate case where this differs from the intended composition, and the definition is already at its natural generality: arbitrary categories A, B, T, arbitrary functors L and R, and arbitrary morphism properties.
